speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to better understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been persisting, and do you smoke or have any other lung exposures?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis

The chronic nature (11 years), copious purulent sputum, and recurrent infections in a non-smoker are highly suggestive of bronchiectasis rather than chronic bronchitis. To confirm this, I need to see your lungs; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CXR and please schedule a Chest_CT for a definitive diagnosis.
